About the Role

As Signal Processing Engineer within RF Processing & Analytics, you own the algorithms that turn raw electromagnetic intercepts into an actionable picture of the RF environment — detecting, characterizing, and identifying the emitters around our platforms in contested environments. You work across the signals captured by our Radar, Radio, and Electronic Warfare modules, building the classification and analytics layer that turns isolated detections into a real-time electronic order of battle for operators and downstream autonomy.

Responsibilities

 - Signal Detection & Characterization: Build algorithms to detect, deinterleave, and extract parameters (PRI, pulse width, frequency, modulation) from intercepted RF emissions.

 - Emitter Classification & Identification: Develop classification pipelines — combining feature-based methods and machine learning — to identify emitter types and match them against threat libraries.

 - Electronic Order of Battle: Design the analytics that turn individual detections into a coherent, real-time picture of emitters, tracks, and threat posture.

 - AI-Assisted Analytics: Apply machine learning to modulation recognition, anomaly detection, and emitter fingerprinting where it improves classification confidence in dense, contested spectrum.

 - Cross-Module Data Fusion: Work with signals captured by Radar, Radio, and Electronic Warfare to build a unified processing pipeline rather than siloed, single-sensor analysis.

 - Real-Time Pipeline Engineering: Take algorithms from offline prototyping (MATLAB/Python) to real-time or near-real-time implementation, alongside software and embedded/FPGA engineers.

 - Field Validation: Validate detection and classification performance against simulated and real-world RF datasets, in lab and field-test conditions.

 - 3-6 years of experience in RF/radar signal processing, ideally with exposure to ELINT, ESM, or SIGINT applications.

 - Proficiency in Python and/or MATLAB for algorithm prototyping; working knowledge of C/C++ for production-oriented implementation.

 - Build synthetic data pipelines that generate, filter, and curate training and evaluation samples for complex legal reasoning and agentic workflows.

 - Build and maintain capability benchmarks like our Legal Agent Benchmark (LAB), along with product-focused evals that track how models perform on real customer workflows.

 - Work with legal domain experts to define quality metrics, rubrics, and other grading mechanisms for training and evaluation.

 - Own training and evaluation data quality, including provenance, coverage, and safeguards against contamination.

 - Close the loop from product usage and customer feedback to new evaluations and training data, so models improve where customers need them most.

 - Partner with researchers to investigate model failures, distinguish real gains from misleading metrics, and use findings to guide training and release decisions.

 - The ability to translate ambiguous goals or expert judgment into structured datasets, rubrics, and measurable criteria.

 - Experience with synthetic data, LLM evaluations, automated raters, or preference data is a plus. Strong data and measurement engineering experience close to ML model development is valuable even without prior LLM work.

jobs.title: Machine Controls & Data Integration System Engineer, Additive Manufacturing
jobs.description:
HADRIAN - MANUFACTURING THE FUTURE

Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.

Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.

Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.

If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.

What You'll Do

 - Machine Connectivity Across the Fleet: Build and own the connectivity layer across the AM fleet — PC-based machine control systems, PLC-based subsystems, and vendor interfaces alike — including the log, file, and tag-level extraction required where no standard interface exists.

 - Canonical Data Model and Schema Governance: Own the schemas, tag dictionaries, naming conventions, units, and versioning that let one integration pattern scale across platforms and sites. Govern schema change so downstream consumers do not break.

 - Pipelines and Storage: Design, build, and operate the telemetry and build data pipelines — transport, stream processing, buffering, and persistence into relational and time-series storage — with the uptime, backfill, and data integrity guarantees that qualification evidence depends on.

 - Machine State Models and OPUS Integration: Own how a machine reports what it is doing, how work is dispatched to it, and how each build record ties to part, powder lot, machine, and operator for end-to-end traceability.

 - Requirements and Interface Baseline: Define the interface, control, and data requirements; flow them down to OEMs and to internal engineering; verify what is delivered against them; and hold the change-controlled interface control documents — state models, command semantics, telemetry dictionaries, alarm and error handling, and version history — so every integration is specified before it is built, reproducible across machines and sites, and enforceable with vendors as their platforms and firmware evolve.

 - Supplementary Instrumentation: Instrument what the OEM does not expose. Specify and integrate supplementary sensing, edge compute, and data acquisition where native machine data is insufficient for process monitoring or engineering investigation.

 - OT Network and Controller Accreditation: Partner with IT and Security to get machine controllers onto a compliant network — segmentation, remote access, patch and firmware change paths, and controller accreditation under NIST SP 800-171 and CMMC.

 - Safety State Integration: Integrate machine and cell safety state into the control and platform layer, and validate interlock behavior against aerospace and defense production requirements, in coordination with the Automation & Robotics Engineer and site EHS.

 - Commissioning and Acceptance Support: Support commissioning, Factory Acceptance Test (FAT), and Site Acceptance Test (SAT) from a controls and connectivity standpoint, ensuring each machine meets the Hadrian integration standard before production release.

 - Build Preparation Toolchain Handoff: Support the build preparation and slicing toolchain integration path — the handoff from build preparation software into machine execution and back into the manufacturing record — in partnership with Application Engineering and the software team.

 - OEM Technical Relationships: Establish and maintain OEM relationships covering interface and data access, controller and firmware change management, calibration hooks, and serviceability — including holding vendors to the agreed interface requirements through platform and firmware changes.

Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. jobs.title: Senior Data Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT HALTER

At Halter, we’re on a mission to enable farmers and graziers to run the most productive and sustainable operations. Our customers are using Halter to break free from the time-intensive constraints of conventional practices. Imagine watching 500 cattle stand up and walk calmly towards their next break? No quad bikes, no dogs, no fences. Just a group of cattle walking at their own pace. People say it looks like magic. Our customers are revolutionizing grazing with Halter. It's changing lives and transforming an industry. People join Halter to do meaningful work. By joining us you’ll be solving challenging problems within a talented team and a culture built for high performance. Our team out-think, out-work and out-care. We’re committed to delivering real change in the world - this isn’t easy, and in truth, we love that it’s hard. 

We’re backed to deliver on a mission that matters by Tier 1 investors including Founders Fund https://foundersfund.com, Bessemer Venture Partners https://www.bvp.com/, BOND, https://www.bondcap.com/ DCVC https://www.dcvc.com/, Blackbird https://www.blackbird.vc/, Promus Ventures https://www.promusventures.com/, Rocket Lab’s Peter Beck and Icehouse ventures https://www.icehouseventures.co.nz/?utm_term=icehouse%20ventures&utm_campaign=Brand+Keywords&utm_source=adwords&utm_medium=ppc&hsa_acc=4064636360&hsa_cam=16902737884&hsa_grp=134004309485&hsa_ad=592971340272&hsa_src=g&hsa_tgt=kwd-1082530126230&hsa_kw=icehouse%20ventures&hsa_mt=b&hsa_net=adwords&hsa_ver=3&gclid=Cj0KCQjw2v-gBhC1ARIsAOQdKY0J0DepRVFDmjQlAkJPbZuQnLSA5UVzUzOXYiPxkjX-SeVa513_BhkaAr-MEALw_wcB.

To find out more, visit our LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/halter-limited & Instagram https://www.instagram.com/lifeathalter/.

At Halter, data is the lifeblood of everything we build. Every second, collars stream behavioural, location, and health signals from cows in paddocks across the globe. Pair that with remote sensing, grazing data and pasture cover, and you have the foundation for helping farmers make smarter decisions every single day. But that's only one piece. Internally, we rely on production data from our manufacturing floor, field performance data from collars in the wild, and product analytics to shape how we build and scale. 

ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for a Data Engineer with strong backend instincts to join our Data Engineering team to build the pipelines that make all of this work together. Day-to-day you'll partner closely with our machine learning, product, and platform teams to design systems that are reliable, observable, and ready for what's next. Whether it's optimising ingestion for billions of daily events, building robust transformation layers, connecting disparate data sources into a coherent whole, or ensuring data quality at scale you'll own problems end-to-end. If you want your work to have a tangible impact on how the world farms, this is the role for you.

WHAT YOU’LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR

 - Design, build, and maintain scalable data pipelines that move data reliably from source to insight.

 - Own data modelling decisions: clean schemas, sensible abstractions, and infrastructure that scales with the business.

 - Work closely with machine learning, product, and platform teams to ensure data is accessible, accurate, and ready when they need it.

 - Apply AI tools (like Claude Code or Cursor) to improve velocity while keeping pipelines easy to understand and evolve.Champion data quality by building validation, monitoring, and alerting so issues surface before they cause problems downstream.

 - Help define and evolve data practices and standards across the organisation, balancing pragmatic delivery with long-term maintainability.

 - Support and mentor other engineers through design conversations, code reviews, and generous context sharing.

 - Stay hands-on, helping shape not just the plumbing, but the data products that drive decisions.Contribute to the reliability and freshness of our data systems, especially when things get tricky at scale.

 - Help evolve our testing strategies, CI/CD workflows, and infrastructure patterns for data.

WHO WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - You have strong experience building and maintaining data pipelines for mission-critical systems, with a solid grasp of batch and streaming patterns.You have a confident understanding of data engineering best practices: modelling, transformation, orchestration, and quality assurance.

 - You're familiar with cloud infrastructure, ideally AWS. We use Athena, S3, Kinesis, SQS, and SNS, but experience with similar tools translates well.

 - You understand how to build systems that are observable, testable, and easy to debug

 - You're a product-minded engineer. You care about why we're building something, not just how.

 - You embrace ambiguity. At Halter, the problems worth solving rarely come with a clear spec. You're comfortable navigating uncertainty and making pragmatic calls.

 - You're deeply curious and motivated by impact. Bonus points if you're genuinely interested in agriculture, but what matters most is that you want your work to matter.

 - You're a highly effective collaborator. You lift the people around you through clear communication, generous knowledge sharing, and a low ego.

 - Importantly, we're looking for someone who is passionate about what they do and eager to learn.

OUR BENEFITS

 - Importantly, we offer an inclusive and attractive remuneration package made up of salary, benefits and an employee stock ownership plan.

 - Healthy body, healthy mind. We’re partnered with Southern Cross Health Insurance to support your well-being.

 - Our personal growth is important. Halter offers an annual $1000 self-development budget to be used for anything that fuels personal growth.

 - We offer 6 months of fully paid parental leave for primary caregivers, 4 weeks of fully paid secondary caregiver leave and many other parental benefits that support you and your family.

 - Our time to recharge is valued, we’re offered wellness leave and unlimited paid annual leave.

OUR OFFICE FIRST APPROACH

There’s a reason you visit your friends in person, live with your family and don’t do dinners over Zoom. Humans are wired for connection. We believe a world-class, in-person office culture is the best way for high-performing teams.

Being office first is a core pillar of our culture. We believe in-person connections are key to driving your own growth, learning, impact, and building genuine long-lasting relationships. Strong relationships make it easier to disagree, give feedback, and do meaningful and aligned work. We don’t like having heaps of rules or policies, but this means having strong, trusted relationships is critical.

We’re office first, not office only. This means working from the office everyday is our default setting, but we flex when we need to. We have a high-trust culture, so everyone is trusted to do what’s best for Halter.

Our office vibe is something special, it’s hard to describe until you’re here, but people at Halter who have come from fully remote or hybrid companies say they could never go back - the high energy and spectacular people they are now surrounded by everyday makes work so enjoyable. Your growth, your learning and your impact is truly unlimited here, and a big part of that comes from being together solving problems, innovating, building context, and constantly learning from each other.

JOIN OUR TEAM

Halter is committed to promoting a diverse and inclusive workplace — a place where we can each be ourselves and do the best work of our lives. Research shows that while men apply to jobs when they meet an average of 60% of the requirements, women and under-represented groups of candidates tend to only apply when they meet every requirement. If you think you have what it takes but don’t necessarily tick every requirement on this job description, please still get in touch and apply to Halter. We’d love to chat to see if you’ll be an epic fit!

If this opportunity sounds like you, please apply below by sending through your cover letter explaining why you’re excited about this role and working at Halter, along with your CV, and we’ll be in touch!

Please also feel free to check out the careers page https://www.halterhq.com/careers for more information on working at Halter and don't forget to follow us on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/halter-limited & Instagram https://www.instagram.com/lifeathalter/.

WHY OUR TEAM LOVES WORKING AT HALTER:

 - Work that genuinely matters. Every now and again a company comes along that transforms an entire industry and leaves the world in a better place. Our team gets to be part of something truly meaningful, helping farmers improve their livelihoods, spend more time with their families, and build more sustainable operations.

 - Spectacular people solving hard problems. Our culture is designed for talented people to do work that changes lives. The team is filled with diverse, kind, and driven people who push each other to do their best work. You'll be thrown into the deep end, tackling complex challenges and building something tangible that solves real problems.

 - You'll grow here. Autonomy, mastery, and learning define how we work. You'll have the freedom to work on interesting problems, master new skills, and continuously develop yourself, both through your role and our personal growth fund.

 - This isn't easy, and we love that it's hard. Working at Halter will be the most rewarding and the most challenging work of your life. We move fast, take bold bets, and work hard to reshape an entire industry. As one team member put it: "Joining Halter is a bit like strapping yourself to a rocket ship, but it's an epic journey to be a part of!"

jobs.title: Infrastructure Software Engineer, AI & Data Security (Contract, Argentina)
jobs.description:
ABOUT HOMEVISION

HomeVision is building the next generation of AI-powered software for the $13 trillion mortgage industry. Our platform, MIRA (Machine Intelligence Review Assistant), automates labor-intensive document processing and underwriting, helping lenders close loans faster and with less friction — ultimately saving borrowers time, money, and stress. We have already transformed appraisal operations for the country's top lenders, cutting review times by over 75%. Now, we are aggressively expanding MIRA to cover the entire loan file — automating income, assets, and credit analysis — to create a holistic underwriting utility for the industry.

We look for hungry, smart, curious and kind people who enjoy hard problems and real responsibility. Engineers own meaningful projects end to end, from design to deployment, and collaborate closely with product, design and our go-to-market teams. We value low ego, high ownership, clear communication, and respect for each other's time. We always try to "do the loving thing" in how we work together and with our customers and partners.

THE ROLE

This is a mixed Software Engineering and Infrastructure role at the intersection of AI and data security. As we expand MIRA across the entire loan file, our hardest challenges shift from model building to the infrastructure needed to securely develop, test and run AI systems. You'll drive that infrastructure. It's a backend engineering role where you will work in application code as well as in Terraform/AWS with a security-first mindset.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Plan, design, and build

 - Secure infrastructure for AI-assisted development and testing

 - Data-access security across the platform

 - Cross-cutting application features

You will manage your own projects, communicating designs, plans, and status updates proactively. We work in Go, Python, and TypeScript with a focus on reliability and observability.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING

• Strong backend software engineering experience

• A security-first mindset: you naturally consider data access and potential leak vectors for every process, person, and agent.

• Genuine interest in AI/LLM systems and the infrastructure that makes them safe and reliable to build on

• Experience and/or a strong interest in working at the infrastructure level with Terraform, AWS, GCP etc

• The ability to take an ambiguous, hard problem from design doc to production

• Strong verbal and written communication in English

BONUS POINTS

• Experience with Infrastructure-as-Code (Terraform) and observability tooling (e.g. Datadog)

• Experience designing infrastructure on AWS — isolation/sandboxing, networking, and the primitives that keep systems secure under real load

• Residence in Rosario or Buenos Aires (Residence in Argentina is mandatory)

WHAT WE'LL OFFER YOU

• A competitive salary in USD

• A high degree of autonomy and ownership of your work

• Support for your professional goals and learning within and beyond the company, through your manager and peers

NOTES
Recruiter and AI submissions will be rejected.
All hires will be subject to thorough criminal, education, work history, and reference checks.
Compensation is DOE.

jobs.title: Senior Database Reliability Engineer - Global Infrastructure
jobs.description:
At i3D.net http://i3D.net, we provide world-class global coverage with one of the most interconnected networks in the world. Our solutions focus on low latency, zero packet loss, and unmatched scalability, enabling seamless experiences for millions of users worldwide. With dedicated support, bespoke solutions, and cutting-edge technology, we deliver reliable, cost-efficient infrastructure that empowers game developers and businesses to scale effortlessly. Partnering with major names like Nvidia, DuckDuckGo, and Ubisoft, we are shaping the future of gaming and network technology.

WHY YOUR ROLE MATTERS

As a Senior Database Reliability Engineer, you own the availability, scalability, and performance of our MariaDB/MySQL platforms that power real time and latency sensitive services across i3D.net http://i3D.net's global infrastructure.

You design, build, and operate highly available database platforms that are reliable, observable, and easy for our internal engineering teams to consume. From provisioning new database clusters and automating operations to improving performance and supporting mission critical production workloads, you play a key role in ensuring our services remain fast, resilient, and always available.

Because i3D.net http://i3D.net operates its own global infrastructure, you work across the full technology stack. Alongside database engineering, you'll work closely with Linux, Kubernetes, Infrastructure-as-Code, and platform automation to build modern database services rather than simply administer databases.

WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING

 - Design and build database platforms: You design, build, and evolve highly available RDBMS platforms, ensuring they are resilient, scalable, and aligned with platform standards across multiple environments.

 - Operate and optimize database clusters: You manage multi-environment database clusters, including replication, failover, backups, and performance tuning, using components such as Kubernetes and load balancers.

 - Automate database operations: You automate database provisioning, configuration, upgrades, and maintenance using IaC, reducing manual effort and increasing consistency across environments.

 - Linux and systems ownership: You take responsibility for the Linux systems running database workloads, handling day-to-day operations, troubleshooting, and system-level tuning in bare metal and hybrid setups.

 - CI/CD for database platforms: You integrate database changes into CI/CD pipelines, supporting safe and repeatable deployments, schema changes, and configuration updates across staging and production.

 - Monitoring and observability: You implement and maintain monitoring and alerting for database platforms using tools such as Prometheus and Grafana, ensuring clear visibility into performance, capacity, and reliability.

 - Security and reliability: You apply security best practices to database platforms, including access control, encryption, and compliance requirements, while continuously improving availability and recovery processes.

 - Collaboration and knowledge sharing: You work closely with platform, DevOps, and application teams, sharing knowledge, improving internal tooling, and supporting incident reviews and continuous improvement.

TECH STACK

At i3D.net http://i3D.net, you’ll work with:

 - Databases: MariaDB/MySQL, multi-node clusters, replication, backups and recovery

 - Infrastructure and tooling: Linux (bare metal and hybrid), Docker, Kubernetes, Ansible, GitHub Actions

 - Observability: Prometheus, Grafana, logging and alerting stacks

 - Practices: Infrastructure as Code, CI/CD, Agile ways of working, you build it, you deploy it, you support it.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE IN THE FIRST YEAR

 - Database platforms are stable, scalable and consumable by our systems and teams

 - Manual database operations are largely automated

 - Performance and availability issues are detected earlier and resolved faster

 - Backup, recovery, and failover processes are reliable and well tested

 - You are a trusted point of knowledge for database and platform topics within the team

YOUR PROFILE

 - Database Engineering experience: You have 5+ years of hands-on experience managing production database platforms, preferably MariaDB, MySQL and PostgreSQL, with strong requirements around uptime, performance, and data integrity.

 - Linux & Kubernetes: You are comfortable operating Linux systems, especially in on-premise or hybrid environments, and regularly troubleshoot issues spanning storage, networking, and system resources.

 - Automation and Infrastructure-as-Code: You use tools like Ansible and Terraform to automate database and infrastructure workflows and avoid manual configuration wherever possible.

 - CI/CD and platform integration: You have experience integrating databases into CI/CD pipelines and working alongside application and platform teams to support reliable releases. Experience with GitHub Actions is a plus.

 - Monitoring and observability: You have worked with Prometheus and Grafana in production environments and understand how to monitor database health, performance, and capacity effectively.

 - Collaboration and mindset: You enjoy working in platform or SRE style teams, contributing to documentation and tooling, and supporting others through reviews, incidents, and shared learning.

 - Remote vs onsite: This is a hybrid role, so you'll spend some time working onsite at our Rotterdam office. If you're already in the Netherlands, great. If not, we're happy to support your move with our relocation services (a valid EU work permit is required).

WHY JOIN US?

 - Global Impact: Help build and operate our internal platform on our own hardware, deployed across multiple data centers worldwide, with a focus on performance, scalability, and reliability.

 - Innovation at Scale: Drive the orchestration and automation of our bare-metal platform, ensuring full control, scalability, and high performance across global deployments.

 - Hybrid Work Setup: Enjoy the flexibility of a hybrid role with a work-from-home budget and top-tier tools.

 - Career Growth: Access to education reimbursement, career guidance, and opportunities to upskill.

 - Competitive Perks: Annual bonus, Generous PTO, travel allowance, pension plan.

 - Free Games: Enjoy lifetime access to Ubisoft’s game library

jobs.description:
Get to Know Us

Horizon3 http://Horizon3.ai is a fast-growing, remote cybersecurity company dedicated to the mission of enabling organizations to proactively find, fix and verify exploitable attack vectors before criminals exploit them. Our flagship product, the NodeZeroTM platform, delivers production-safe autonomous pentests and other key assessment operations that scale across the largest internal, external, cloud, and hybrid cloud environments. NodeZero has been adopted by organizations of all sizes, from small educational institutions to government agencies and Global 100 enterprises. It is used by IT Ops/SecOps teams, consulting pentesters, and MSSPs and MSPs.

We are a fusion of former U.S. Special Operations cyber operators, startup engineers & operators, and formerly frustrated cybersecurity practitioners. We're committed to helping solve our common security problems: ineffective security tools and false positives, resulting in alert fatigue, blind spots, "checkbox” security culture, cybersecurity skills shortage, and the long lead time and expense of hiring outside consultants. Collectively, we are a team of learn it alls, committed to a culture of respect, collaboration, ownership, and results.

As a remote first company, we require minimum 25Mbps consumer grade broadband connection.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

The Pentest Data Platform (PDP) team owns the shared data platform that ingests NodeZero output from ephemeral operations and delivers it into durable storage, increasingly, in near real time. The team's core mandate is to build a scalable, event-driven architecture that makes operational insights available in near real-time, not just after it finishes.

PDP is a foundational, platform-oriented team whose outputs power core user experiences within the NodeZero security platform. PDP owns the data contracts and internal data services that everything else is built on top of.

NodeZero generates large volumes of structured pentest telemetry: hosts, findings, attack paths, credentials, weaknesses, and relationship graphs. PDP is responsible for turning that raw telemetry into coherent, durable, and queryable records that downstream teams can build on reliably at enterprise scale.

The team is driving the largest architectural change in Horizon3's history: reworking pentest data processing from a batch-centric monolith into a real-time, event-driven microservice architecture. There is existing code to understand, live customers to protect, and hard distributed-systems problems to solve, all at the same time.

In this role, you will:

 - Own event-driven pipelines end to end — design, build, and operate streaming services that ingest, distribute, and process pentest operation results, including streaming and batch ETL, aggregation services, schema migrations, and replayable processing.

 - Solve real-time asset identity problems — work on asset matching, asset counting, and cross-operation reconciliation, including reducing false splits and overcounting, improving matching explainability, and making asset identity available while an operation is running rather than only after completion.

 - Evolve the data model — manage durable SQL-backed storage (PostgreSQL), drive schema evolution with zero-regression fidelity, and ensure data correctness, idempotency, and reliable reprocessing and failure handling.

 - Drive enterprise scalability — own database performance, connection pooling, resource management, and platform reliability for a system that must handle hundreds of thousands of hosts per customer.

jobs.description:
Get to Know Us

Horizon3.ai http://Horizon3.ai is a fast-growing, remote cybersecurity company dedicated to the mission of enabling organizations to proactively find, fix and verify exploitable attack vectors before criminals exploit them. Our flagship product, the NodeZero™ platform, delivers production-safe autonomous pentests and other key assessment operations that scale across the largest internal, external, cloud, and hybrid cloud environments. NodeZero has been adopted by organizations of all sizes, from small educational institutions to government agencies and Global 100 enterprises. It is used by IT Ops/SecOps teams, consulting pentesters, and MSSPs and MSPs.

We are a fusion of former U.S. Special Operations cyber operators, startup engineers & operators, and formerly frustrated cybersecurity practitioners. We're committed to helping solve our common security problems: ineffective security tools and false positives, resulting in alert fatigue, blind spots, "checkbox" security culture, cybersecurity skills shortage, and the long lead time and expense of hiring outside consultants. Collectively, we are a team of learn-it-alls, committed to a culture of respect, collaboration, ownership, and results.

As a remote first company, we require minimum 25Mbps consumer grade broadband connection.

What You'll Do

The Principal Engineer for Database Platform is the technical anchor of NodeZero's data infrastructure. This is an individual contributor role with no direct reports — your influence is through technical leadership, architecture ownership, and raising the engineering bar across the team. You own the most consequential database architecture decisions, define the standards that govern how NodeZero stores, queries, and migrates data at scale, and ensure the data layer can support NodeZero's growth — more customers, larger environments, more pentest data — without requiring proportional operational effort. This is a deeply hands-on role: you will write code, author design documents, and set the technical direction that every engineer on the Database Platform team builds toward.

NodeZero's data layer is not simple. We store millions of discovered assets, graph-structured attack paths, time-series vulnerability data, and audit-critical pentest results — across a multi-tenant architecture where correctness and data isolation are non-negotiable. You will be the person who makes the hardest data architecture calls and ensures the team has the technical foundations to build reliably on.

 - Technical Strategy: Define and drive the technical roadmap for the Database Platform in partnership with the Senior Engineering Manager and the broader Pentest Platform organization.

 - Architecture Leadership: Own the most complex database architecture decisions — schema design, partitioning strategies, migration patterns, and scalability approaches. Produce design documents that become the shared technical model for the team.

 - PostgreSQL Excellence: Be NodeZero's definitive expert on PostgreSQL at scale — query optimization, indexing, partitioning, replication, and connection pooling. Set the standards the team follows and catch the problems others miss.

 - Graph & Multi-model Data: Architect and guide the evolution of NodeZero's graph-based asset model — the data structure that represents how discovered hosts, services, credentials, and vulnerabilities relate to each other across pentests.

 - Schema Governance: Own schema design review processes. Ensure every migration is safe, reversible, and zero-downtime. Build the tooling and culture that treats schema changes with the same rigor as production code changes.

 - Mentorship & Bar Raising: Mentor P5 and P4 engineers through code review, design review, and pairing. Be the person on the team that raises everyone else's ceiling.

 - Cross-functional Influence: Partner with Data Ingestion, Asset Inventory, API Platform, and Security Research to define data contracts, query performance standards, and architectural guardrails that span the full data pipeline.

What You'll Bring

Technical Depth

 - Deep, production-proven PostgreSQL expertise: query planner internals, advanced indexing (partial, expression, GiST/GIN), partitioning strategies, logical replication, vacuuming at scale, and connection pool tuning.

 - Experience architecting multi-tenant databases at scale: row-level security, tenant isolation, schema-per-tenant vs. shared-schema tradeoffs.

 - Experience with schema migration at scale in production systems: zero-downtime migrations, backwards-compatible schema evolution, and migration tooling (Flyway, golang-migrate, or equivalent).

 - Familiarity with graph data models and graph databases (Neo4j, AWS Neptune) or graph-like query patterns in relational systems (recursive CTEs, ltree, adjacency list).

 - Proficient in Go or Python — able to write production application code, not just SQL.

Architecture & Design

 - Demonstrated track record of defining database architecture at scale — from design doc to production — across multiple companies or teams.

 - Strong opinions on data architecture tradeoffs: normalization vs. denormalization, consistency vs. availability, OLTP vs. OLAP workload separation, and schema-first vs. schema-last design.

 - Able to reason about long-horizon schema design: what does this schema look like in two years, at 10× the current data volume, with three new feature teams writing to it?

 - Able to communicate complex database decisions clearly in writing — for design docs, ADRs, and cross-team reviews — so engineers without deep DB expertise can understand and apply the reasoning.

Leadership Without Authority

 - Proven ability to drive database standards across multiple teams without direct reporting authority — including teams that are not the Database Platform team.

 - Experience establishing database engineering culture: schema review norms, migration safety standards, and query performance review processes.

 - Track record of growing engineers through code review, pair programming, and architectural mentorship — especially engineers who are strong in application code but earlier in their database expertise.

Nice to Haves

 - Background in cybersecurity data: vulnerability databases, network scan schemas, or attack surface management data models.

 - Experience with time-series databases (TimescaleDB, InfluxDB) in addition to relational.

 - Familiarity with data platform compliance requirements: SOC 2 Type II, FedRAMP data handling, or GDPR/CCPA.

 - Experience with analytical query patterns or BI/reporting workloads on operational data.

 - Contributions to open-source database tooling or PostgreSQL ecosystem projects.

Travel Required

We are a fully remote company, and this job may require up to 5% of travel to be successful.

Our compensation structure is designed to be fair, competitive, and transparent, ensuring that every team member is recognized and compensated equitably across roles, levels, and locations.

jobs.title: Research Engineer, Synthetic Data
jobs.description:
ABOUT HUD

HUD https://www.hud.ai/'s mission is to build reliable, fair and open infrastructure for AI data. We want data to be valuable for the people who create it and trustworthy for the labs that train on it. Our team is a quickly growing group of researchers, engineers and operators building the economy that shapes what AI will become. Backed by $16M from top VCs and YC (W25), our marketplace and platform are used by startups, Fortune 500 companies and frontier labs.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for Research Engineers to build our synthetic data pipeline. You’ll turn domain-specific workflows into synthetic training tasks that are realistic enough to enough to teach useful behavior, structured enough to generate at scale, and difficult enough to expand model capabilities.

RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Work with subject-matter experts to create synthetic tasks for training AI agents across a range of professional and technical domains

 - Design synthetic task generation methods that produce diverse, realistic, and learnable tasks

 - Build systems and tooling to mutate, validate, and improve synthetic tasks

 - Analyze model and agent performance on synthetic tasks to understand what the tasks are teaching and where they fail

 - Develop metrics to quantify and understand synthetic task diversity, realism, learnability, etc.

EXPERIENCE

You may be a good fit if you have:

 - Proficiency in Python, Docker, and Linux environments

 - Have experience with synthetic data research methods - please elaborate in your application

 - Strong understanding of what “good synthetic data” means and its limitations

 - Built synthetic data pipelines end-to-end without a fully prescribed roadmap

 - Experience working on environments, evals, and benchmarks

Strong candidates may also:

 - Be detail-oriented and able to spot subtle inconsistencies or edge cases in synthetic data

 - Be able to reason from first principles about task design, scoring, and failure modes

 - Thrive in unstructured problem spaces

 - Early-stage startup experience with ability to work independently in fast-paced environments

 - Strong communication skills for remote collaboration across time zones

We prioritize technical aptitude and learning potential over years of experience. Motivated candidates are encouraged to apply even if they don't meet all criteria.

TEAM & COMPANY DETAILS

 - Team Size: ~25 people currently, mostly full-time in-person, but some remote.

 - Our team: Our team brings together five International Olympiad medalists across IOI, ILO and IPhO, researchers published at NeurIPS and ICLR, and engineers and researchers from Google DeepMind, Amazon, AWS, Meta, Qwen, GLM, and Mercor. It also includes operators from BCG and Uber, the first security hire at one of the largest crypto exchanges, serial AI startup founders, former quant researchers, artists and the former #1 ranked Catan player in the world.

 - Company stage: We have 8 figures in funding and are scaling profitably and quickly to meet very strong demand.

LOGISTICS

 - Employment: Full-time.

 - Location: We have offices in San Francisco or Singapore but are open to remote candidates who can work hours that 70-80% overlap with either San Francisco or Singapore time zones.

 - Visa Sponsorship: We provide support for relocation and visas for strong full-time candidates to the US or Singapore.

 - Timeline: Applications are rolling. The process is 2 technical interviews and a 2-3 day work trial.

WHAT WE OFFER

 - Competitive compensation

 - 100% covered top-of-the-line medical, dental, and vision (US and Singapore employees)

 - Lunch and dinner for in-office employees

 - Company-wide holiday break (Christmas Eve to New Year’s Day) on top of PTO and paid holidays

 - 401k with a 4% match

 - Other perks including an Equinox membership and commuter benefits (US employees) and a health/wellness stipend (Singapore employees)

 - Unlimited* access to tokens for ChatGPT, Claude Code, Cursor, etc. *By unlimited, we mean no one on our token usage leaderboard has ever hit a limit. So we have no idea what the limit is.

 - Two top-floor offices in San Francisco’s Union Square and Singapore’s Raffles Place

 - Annual travel budget to visit either office

COMPENSATION

Actual offers are adjusted for experience and location, but our base salary bands are

 - San Francisco (and other major US cities): $135,000 - $230,000

 - Singapore: $100,000 - $175,000

 - Rest of world: $100,000 - $175,000

Due to high volume, we may not actively respond to every application, but feel free to contact us at recruiting@hud.so or elsewhere if we missed your application!

jobs.title: Senior Staff Data Engineer - Data & ML Platform
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for a Senior Staff Data Engineer to be the technical backbone of our Data & ML Platform team — the foundation powering analytics, product experiences, and machine learning across Hinge Health. This is a high-ownership IC role for someone who wants to set the technical vision for the platform, drive architecture across organizational boundaries, and shape how Hinge Health builds on data and ML for years to come.

Your scope extends beyond any single team or system. You'll own the most consequential architectural decisions across the data platform — how streaming and batch systems converge, how data models serve both analytical and ML workloads, and how the platform evolves as the company's AI ambitions scale. You'll work in a modern stack including Python, SQL, Spark, dbt, Kafka, Flink, Databricks, and AWS, and increasingly at the boundary where data platform meets ML platform — feature pipelines, serving layers, and the infrastructure that makes ML models production-ready.

This is not a role where you go deep on a single system. You'll operate across the full platform surface — identifying the highest-leverage technical problems the organization faces, driving alignment across engineering, Data Science, and product teams, and making architectural decisions that others build on. You should be equally comfortable authoring a platform-wide technical strategy, debugging a production incident, mentoring senior engineers, and explaining tradeoffs to leadership.

WHAT YOU'LL ACCOMPLISH

 - Set the technical vision for the data platform: Own the long-term architectural direction for how streaming and batch systems, data models, and serving layers fit together. Make the architectural decisions that other teams and engineers build on — balancing reliability, performance, cost, and long-term maintainability across the platform.

 - Build at the intersection of data and ML platform: Design the infrastructure that connects the data platform to ML workloads — feature pipelines, feature stores, and serving layers. Partner with Data Science to ensure the data platform produces ML-ready data and supports model training and inference workflows reliably.

 - Raise the engineering bar across the organization: Set standards that extend beyond your immediate team — data modeling patterns, schema governance, testing practices, pipeline reliability, and code quality. Mentor senior engineers, influence engineering culture, and be the technical authority the broader R&D organization looks to on data platform decisions.

 - Drive cross-organizational technical initiatives: Lead complex initiatives that span multiple teams, services, and domains. Define data contracts with upstream services, drive schema evolution strategies, and resolve systemic technical friction between data producers and consumers across the company.

 - Own platform reliability and operational excellence: Drive the reliability posture of the most critical data systems. Lead improvements in observability, data quality, incident response, and cost efficiency at a platform level — making the data foundation trustworthy enough that every team in the organization can build confidently on top of it.

 - Participate in the team’s weekly on-call rotation, helping ensure the reliability and timely support of the systems we build.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS

 - A minimum of 4+ years of hands-on data engineering experience

 - Bachelor’s Degree (or equivalent) in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field.

 - Experience architecting data systems across batch and streaming paradigms, including technologies such as Kafka, Flink, Spark, or equivalent.

 - Strong proficiency in Python and SQL, with deep experience in distributed data processing frameworks and data platform design.

 - Data and ML platform crossover: You've built or contributed to ML platform infrastructure feature pipelines, feature stores, model serving, or MLOps tooling — as a natural extension of your data engineering work. You understand the ML lifecycle well enough to design data systems that serve it effectively.

 - Track record of setting technical direction across an organization — driving alignment across multiple teams, making architectural decisions with broad impact, and delivering outcomes without formal authority.

 - Demonstrated experience mentoring senior engineers and influencing engineering culture and standards beyond your immediate team.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Data Engineering: 10+ years of hands-on data engineering experience, with a significant portion spent in platform or infrastructure roles building systems that other teams depend on.
 Built in a growth-stage environment: Your strongest work was at a mid-sized or scaling company where you had to make foundational architectural decisions — not at a large tech company where the platform was already built.

 - Deep data modeling and governance instincts: You care about schema design, data contracts, and data quality as much as you care about pipeline throughput. You've driven improvements in how upstream services produce data and how downstream teams consume it.

 - Product and business awareness: You connect your technical work to the problems the business is trying to solve. You understand the product use cases your platform enables and use that context to prioritize and make better architectural choices.

 - Operational rigor in regulated environments: You value SLOs, incident management, and observability as first-class concerns. Experience in HIPAA, SOC 2, or similarly regulated environments is a plus.

 - Experience with Databricks ecosystem: Delta Lake, MLflow, Unity Catalog — familiarity with this stack accelerates your impact.

 - AI-forward engineering practices: You actively use AI-assisted development tools and see them as a force multiplier for both your own productivity and the team's.

HINGE HEALTH HYBRID MODEL

We believe that remote work and in-person work have their own advantages and disadvantages, and we want to be able to leverage the best of both worlds. Employees in hybrid roles are required to be in the office 3 days per week, for the full 8 hours of a typical business day. The San Francisco office has a dog-friendly workplace program.

At Hinge Health, we’re using technology to scale and automate the delivery of healthcare, starting with musculoskeletal (MSK) conditions, which affect over 1.7 billion people worldwide. jobs.title: Principal Data Engineer
jobs.description:
Hims & Hers is the leading health and wellness platform, on a mission to help the world feel great through the power of better health. We are redefining healthcare by putting the customer first and delivering access to care that is affordable, accessible, and personal, from diagnosis to treatment to delivery. No two people are the same, so we provide access to personalized care designed for results. By normalizing health & wellness challenges and innovating on their solutions, we’re making better health outcomes easier to achieve. 

Hims & Hers is a public company, traded on the NYSE under the ticker symbol “HIMS.” To learn more about the brand and offerings, you can visit hims.com/about http://hims.com/about and hims.com/how-it-works http://hims.com/how-it-works . For information on the company’s outstanding benefits, culture, and its talent-first flexible/remote work approach, see below and visit www.hims.com/careers-professionals http://www.hims.com/careers-professionals.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

We're hiring a Principal Data Engineer to set the technical direction for data at Hims & Hers. This is the most senior individual contributor role in Data Platform Engineering (DPE), and the scope is deliberately larger than DPE: the architecture you define determines how Software Engineering, Analytics Engineering, and Data Science build on data for millions of patients across our Telehealth, prescription, and wellness products.

The platform runs on GCP BigQuery, Airflow on Astronomer/EKS, dbt, Confluent Kafka, Databricks Delta Lake, and Terraform/OpenTofu. Two foundational pieces are being built from scratch right now: a streaming platform and a lower environments strategy. The most consequential open question is whether streaming stays scoped to analytics or extends into production and model evaluation paths that other teams depend on. That call is yours to make, and the company will live with it for years.

We have Staff engineers who own domains and ship them well. What we don't have is a single person accountable for whether those domains add up to a coherent platform and for whether the bets we're placing now still look right in five years. That's this role.

YOU WILL:

 - The multi-year platform architecture. Ingestion, streaming, orchestration, transformation, and serving as one system rather than five. You decide what we build, what we buy, what we deprecate, and in what order.

 - The streaming bet. Whether Kafka to Flink to BigQuery stays an analytics pipeline or becomes production infrastructure, and what that commits us to operationally, financially, and organizationally. You are the architect of the answer you choose.

 - The contracts between organizations. The interfaces, service boundaries, and data contracts govern how other teams consume from and write into the platform. Where your standards end and another org's autonomy begins is a boundary you define with the VP of Data, not one handed to you.

 - What "trustworthy data" means here, and who is on the hook for it. You define the quality and freshness guarantees the platform makes, the tiering that determines which datasets get them, and the accountability model when they're missed. Staff engineers build the detection, validation, and alerting systems. You decide what we promise, to whom, and at what cost.

 - The economics of the platform. The design decisions that determine what data costs us at scale (storage and compute strategy, reservation model, orchestration footprint) and the accountability framework that keeps consumption honest as more teams build on it. You set the framework. You don't tune every query.

 - The self service strategy. What capabilities let Analytics Engineering and Data Science move without waiting on DPE, what guardrails keep that from breaking production, and how the platform stops being a bottleneck as demand grows faster than headcount.

 - The standards the discipline runs on. Testing, CI/CD, observability, schema governance, and infrastructure as code practice, adopted by teams that don't report to you because the standards are good rather than because you can compel them.

 - Architecture Review. You chair it, and you are the decision-maker of record for cross-team, multi-system, and cost-impacting changes, including ones that touch systems you don't own.

 - The seams between data and everything else. ML and Data Science readiness, HIPAA and PHI compliance posture with Legal and Security, and infrastructure hardening with DevOps. Nobody else is looking at all four at once.

 - The written record. ADRs, design docs, and RFCs that other teams cite as the reference. If a decision only exists in your head, you haven't finished making it.

 - The technical ceiling of the org. Mentorship, design review, and hands-on pairing that makes Staff and Senior engineers better. Part of how you'll measure your impact is the volume of decisions you no longer have to make yourself.

 - You stay hands-on throughout. You write and review production code, and you're in the room for platform-level P1s, driving the systemic fix rather than owning the runbook. This is a technical authority role, not an advisory one.

YOU HAVE:

 - 15+ years building and owning data platform architecture, with a record of decisions whose consequences you stayed to live with, ideally across multiple companies or multiple platform generations

 - Evidence you've set technical direction for organizations you didn't manage, and got adoption through credibility rather than reporting lines

 - Experience defining the edges of your own architectural authority. Ambiguity about where your mandate ends should not stall you

 - Deep GCP and BigQuery expertise, plus real operational fluency in AWS (our Airflow runs on EKS). Multicloud is the job here, not a bonus

 - Modern data stack at platform scale: governing dbt across teams, Airflow/Astronomer, Kafka/Confluent, Databricks/Spark, Fivetran, and reverse ETL or activation platforms such as Hightouch

 - Event streaming in production at scale, including Schema Registry, data contracts, consumer lag management, and delivery semantics along with what they actually cost. Bonus if you've personally made the analytics versus production streaming call

 - Data governance and compliance in a regulated environment: HIPAA and PHI handling, data classification, access controls, audit logging, and GDPR

 - Terraform or equivalent, and the conviction that infrastructure changes are software changes

 - Strong Python and SQL. You raise the bar on production pipeline code by reviewing it, not by talking about it

 - Writing that creates alignment across organizations. Your design docs are where decisions get made, not summaries of decisions already made elsewhere

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

 - Databricks, Unity Catalog, and Delta Lake in production at scale

 - CDC patterns and Flink for real-time processing, particularly where streaming infrastructure served both analytics and production or model serving paths across multiple teams

 - PySpark and SparkSQL for large-scale batch and streaming workloads

 - A BigQuery to Databricks Lakehouse migration, or an equivalent warehouse migration you led end-to-end

 - MLOps partnership: model training pipelines, feature stores, experimentation infrastructure, or the data foundations behind AI-driven product features

 - Go or Python service development for Kafka producers and consumers

 - Direct-to-consumer healthcare or telehealth with HIPAA and GDPR obligations

 - SOX compliance controls in a data engineering context

OUR BENEFITS (THERE ARE MORE BUT HERE ARE SOME HIGHLIGHTS):

 - Competitive salary & equity compensation for full-time roles

 - Unlimited PTO, company holidays, and quarterly mental health days

 - Comprehensive health benefits including medical, dental & vision, and parental leave

 - Employee Stock Purchase Program (ESPP)

 - 401k benefits with employer matching contribution

 - Offsite team retreats

We are committed to building a workforce that reflects diverse perspectives and prioritizes ethics, wellness, and a strong sense of belonging. If you're excited about this role, we encourage you to apply—even if you're not sure if your background or experience is a perfect match.

jobs.title: Staff Data Platform Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT INSCRIBE

At Inscribe, we're on a mission to catch fraud with confidence. In 2017, we set out to build the first document fraud detection product. Today, we process millions of applications each year and work with many of the leading fintechs and banks across the U.S. We believe the game of cat-and-mouse in fraud requires a fundamentally new approach. With care for our customers, attention to detail, and grounded execution, we’re reimagining how fraud is detected and prevented.

Inscribe is trusted by leading banks and fintechs, including Coinbase, Plaid, Bluevine, and Ramp. Inscribe is backed by Threshold Ventures, Uncork Capital, Y Combinator, Crosslink Capital, and Foundry, and is headquartered in San Francisco, CA.

The Opportunity
Inscribe is scaling quickly, and our platform sits at the heart of our customers’ fraud workflows. Every document we analyse and every real-time API decision depends on datastores that are fast, available, and built to grow. We’re hiring a Staff Data Platform Engineer to own how we run, scale, and deploy our databases in the cloud.

This role blends database engineering, site reliability, cloud architecture, and platform automation. You’ll own the reliability and performance of our data layer, from query plans and indexing to replication, failover, backups, and cost. You’ll make sure that as customer volumes and data grow, our datastores stay fast, stable, and cost-efficient.

We’re looking for a high-agency engineer who can assess our data infrastructure today, find what won’t scale, and fix it in line with business goals. This is a hands-on role for someone who thinks in systems, treats databases as a product for other engineers, and raises the bar for data reliability across the company.

Responsibilities

 - Own the design, operation, and scaling of our datastores (Postgres, Redis) on AWS, including provisioning, configuration, replication, high availability, and disaster recovery.

 - Lead datastore optimization: query and index tuning, schema design, connection pooling, caching strategies, and maintenance work such as vacuuming, bloat management, and partitioning.

 - Plan and carry out database scaling as data volumes grow, using read replicas, partitioning, archival, sharding, and horizontal scaling where needed, ahead of demand rather than in response to incidents.

 - Define and run database reliability practices: SLOs for the data layer, backup and point-in-time recovery testing, failover drills, defined RPO/RTO targets, and incident runbooks.

 - Optimize deployment pipelines, test environments, and release automation to improve developer efficiency and reduce operational risk, including safe zero-downtime schema migrations and realistic test databases.

 - Manage cloud database deployments as code with Terraform, standardising how databases are created, configured, upgraded, and retired.

 - Drive cloud optimization for the data tier by rightsizing instances, tuning storage and IOPS, managing reserved capacity, and making cost visible to the teams that create it.

 - Build observability for the data layer in Datadog and Grafana, covering query latency, replication lag, connection saturation, storage growth, and cost, with alerts that are useful to act on.

 - Work with product engineers on data models and access patterns so new features scale from launch.

 - Embed security and compliance controls such as encryption, access management, auditing, and network isolation into how our datastores are run.

 - Lead data infrastructure projects from roadmap through rollout, anchored in business impact and product goals.

 - Mentor teammates and set a high standard for engineering quality, documentation, and operational rigor.

Tech Stack
We don’t expect candidates to know everything, but experience in most of these areas will help:

 - Cloud: AWS (RDS/Aurora, ECS, S3, Bedrock, etc.)

 - Datastores: Postgres, Redis

 - Infrastructure: Terraform, Docker

 - Observability: Datadog, Grafana

 - Languages: Python (Django), SQL

 - AI Platforms: Anthropic, AWS Bedrock

About You
Essential

 - 6+ years of hands-on experience in database reliability engineering, data platform engineering, SRE, or DevOps, with substantial time running production databases.

 - Deep Postgres expertise: query planning, indexing, replication, upgrades, and diagnosing performance problems under real production load.

 - Proven experience scaling datastores in a high-growth environment, including migrations, sharding and capacity planning.

 - Experience deploying and operating managed databases on AWS (or another major cloud) through infrastructure as code.

 - Strong Python skills and comfort working in an application codebase, including ORM-generated queries (Django experience is a plus).

 - Experience building CI/CD and release automation, especially safe schema migrations in continuous delivery.

 - A track record of cutting cloud spend without giving up reliability.

 - A business-aware, pragmatic approach: you connect data infrastructure decisions to product goals and growth, and balance short-term delivery with long-term design.

Highly sought

 - Experience with distributed or horizontally scalable databases (for example Aurora, Citus, CockroachDB, or YugabyteDB).

 - Experience with migration patterns such as CDC and logical replication, with verification and rollback.

 - Experience building internal database tooling or “database-as-a-service” style platforms for product teams.

 - Familiarity with security and compliance requirements for sensitive financial or identity data.

BENEFITS

At Inscribe, we are building a company and culture where everyone can produce their best work. Here are a few of our benefits and perks: 

 - Competitive salary and meaningful equity

 - Comprehensive healthcare

 - Unlimited vacation policy 

 - 401(k) and pension plans

 - Complete work setup 

 - Monthly wellness stipend

jobs.title: Senior Engineering Manager, Infrastructure & Data Engineering
jobs.description:
Today, 67% of students and 82% of low-income students can’t read at grade level by the end of third grade. That’s when students are supposed to go from learning to read to reading to learn. It’s America’s number one education crisis and we know how to fix it.

Ignite Reading delivers one-to-one virtual tutoring that teaches every student the foundational skills they need to become a confident, fluent reader. We pair students who need extra support with expert reading tutors who provide daily, 15-minute, Science of Reading-based instruction that rapidly closes their decoding gaps. We focus on the foundational reading skills—phonics, phonemic awareness, and sight words—kids need to master so they can decode a sentence. Students in Ignite Reading’s program achieve over 2 weeks of reading skills growth per week of instruction, and notably all students achieve the same outstanding results including students with IEPs, multilingual learners, students of color and those receiving free or reduced-price lunch.

Ignite Reading is a mission-driven public benefit corporation. We believe we can do well for our team members and shareholders while we solve one of the nation’s biggest challenges. We believe we will be more successful with a diverse team and are seeking candidates who have lived experience related to social justice, diversity, equity, and inclusion.

YOUR ROLE

Reporting to the Director of Engineering, the Senior Platform Engineering Manager, Infrastructure & Data Engineering owns the platform on which all of Ignite Reading’s engineering and analytics work runs. You will lead two teams — DevOps and Data Engineering (six engineers total) — that together provide the cloud infrastructure, deployment pipelines, and data platform serving a 33-person engineering organization and our Data team.

This is a player-coach role. You will manage and grow experienced engineers, set technical direction across both teams, and stay close enough to the work to review designs, shape architecture, and earn the trust of senior ICs. You will also own our security compliance program — our annual SOC2 audit and penetration test — as a program leader coordinating auditors, vendors, and internal teams.

We don’t expect deep expertise in both infrastructure and data engineering — leaders with that profile are rare, and the role doesn’t require it. We’re looking for real depth in one domain and genuine fluency in the other: enough to guide technical decisions, ask the questions that matter, and know when to lean on your senior engineers.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Lead, manage, and grow two teams: DevOps (cloud infrastructure, CI/CD, observability, incident response) and Data Engineering (pipelines, warehouse, data platform).

 - Provide technical guidance, mentorship, and career development for six engineers, including developing technical leads within each team.

 - Set and drive a unified platform roadmap in partnership with the Director of Engineering and VP of Data, balancing infrastructure investment, data platform direction, and technical debt against delivery needs.

 - Ensure reliable, scalable, secure cloud infrastructure on AWS and smooth, efficient deployment pipelines for the entire engineering organization.

 - Ensure the data platform serves both of its customers well — product engineering and our analytics/data science team — with clear intake, prioritization, and data quality standards.

 - Oversee system monitoring, alerting, on-call, and incident response to maintain high availability and performance.

 - Own the annual SOC2 audit cycle and annual penetration test: planning, evidence collection, vendor and auditor coordination, and remediation tracking.

 - Collaborate with development teams to integrate DevOps and data best practices into the software development lifecycle.

 - Contribute technically — writing and collaborating on technical specifications, reviewing designs, and guiding architectural decisions across both teams.

AI-ENHANCED ENGINEERING LEADERSHIP

 - Model effective use of AI coding and analysis tools (GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Claude, etc.) in your own technical work.

 - Coach both teams on AI-assisted development practices; identify and remove barriers to adoption.

 - Ensure AI-generated code and configuration are validated to meet quality, security, and architecture standards — especially critical in infrastructure and data pipeline contexts.

 - Track and share team-level AI adoption progress, wins, and learnings across the engineering organization.

QUALIFICATIONS

 - 8+ years in software, infrastructure, or data engineering, including 2+ years directly managing engineers (not solely projects or tech leadership).

 - Deep, hands-on expertise in at least one of our two domains: cloud infrastructure/DevOps (AWS, IaC, CI/CD, containerization, observability) or modern data engineering (orchestration, warehousing, pipelines-as-code, data quality).

 - Working fluency in the other domain — able to review designs, guide priorities, and support senior engineers credibly.

 - Experience running a team that serves multiple internal customers, with a track record of transparent prioritization across competing demands.

 - Familiarity with security and compliance standards such as SOC2, and comfort owning a compliance program end-to-end (coordination and program management — not security engineering).

 - Experience developing senior engineers into technical leads and building team resilience (documentation, on-call health, single point of failure reduction).

 - Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively across engineering, data, and business stakeholders.

 - Strategic thinker with the ability to balance short-term objectives with long-term goals.

 - Ability to be self-managing and flexible while working in a remote environment.

AI CODING PROFICIENCY

 - Demonstrated experience using AI coding assistants as a regular part of your development workflow.

 - Ability to effectively validate AI outputs and identify when AI suggestions should be modified or rejected.

 - Understanding of when AI tools add value versus when traditional approaches are more appropriate.

 - Willingness to learn, adapt to, and coach others on new AI development tools and practices.

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

At Ignite Reading, we embrace transparent compensation for a few reasons: to promote fairness and equity, to reduce pay discrimination based on gender, race, or negotiation skill, and to build trust within our team. The same role receives the same compensation — no negotiation.

Salary: $210,000-$220,000

We also ensure you have the tools you need to thrive both in and out of work.

🌴 Unlimited vacation days (+ 12 paid holidays)

jobs.title: Senior Analytics Engineer
jobs.description:
Collections today works like an emergency room. The doctors carry too many patients, everyone arrives at their worst moment, and nobody has their chart. We're making it primary care. January personalizes interactions and optimizes decisions across every stage of consumer credit. We started in the hardest, most broken stage, because if it works there it works anywhere.

Most consumers want to pay what they owe. They want a way out, not a break. We've serviced over $20 billion in debt across more than 20 million consumers. We see more people with charged-off loans each year than all but the top five US banks. Those consumers rate us about 50% higher than the banks that lent them the money. Creditors net over 30% more because we collect more and charge less.

Most AI strips the human out of the work. We use it to make someone's hardest financial moment more human. The more human we make it, the more people recover. Now we're moving upstream, catching people before they default and building across every stage of the consumer credit lifecycle. The consumer in collections today is the consumer who gets approved tomorrow.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As January's Senior Analytics Engineer, you'll own the layer that makes our data trustworthy — for the people who use it today, and for the AI agents that will increasingly use it tomorrow. Data Engineering gets raw data reliably into Snowflake; you take it from there. You'll build and govern our semantic layer, standardize how teams across January define and measure success, and make sure that a metric means the same thing whether it's surfaced on a dashboard, in a Slack chatbot, or by an LLM answering a question on someone's behalf. You'll partner with Data Engineering to deliver impactful client reports, and you'll advocate for the data January needs to capture, but doesn't yet. This is a foundational hire for a company betting that the future of analytics is fewer people writing one-off queries and more trust built into the data itself.

You will:

 - Own the gold layer and build January's semantic layer — designing the dbt-driven, Snowflake-native layer that becomes the single source of truth for every tool that answers a data question, from Sigma to a Slack chatbot to future LLM-based interfaces

 - Define and enforce data contracts and standardized metrics — establishing clear ownership boundaries so gold-layer changes are intentional and communicated, and resolving cross-team disagreement about what a metric means

 - Partner on our client reporting revamp — working alongside Data Engineering (who own the underlying pipeline architecture) to clarify metric definitions, define client success criteria, and build the gold-layer models the new reporting experience needs — including data products clients don't know to ask for yet

 - Advocate to expand the data January captures — partnering with Analytics, Borrower Support, and Client Acquisition to close data-capture gaps (event granularity, structured conversational data, richer client attributes) that limit what your models can do

 - Own cost management for dbt, Snowflake compute powering the gold layer, and analytics tooling like Sigma

 - Enable trustworthy self-service — building certified, well-documented data products that let analysts, PMs, and ops teams (and eventually agents) get correct answers without pinging a data scientist

 - Deliver immediate impact through key projects, including:

 - Semantic Layer Buildout: Design and ship the first version of January's Snowflake-native semantic layer, feeding Sigma, internal tools, and future chatbot/LLM interfaces from a single certified source

 - Metrics Standardization: Resolve the highest-friction metric definition conflicts across teams and establish a durable process (a metrics registry or equivalent) to prevent recurrence

 - Advanced SQL skills, with a track record of modeling data for both flexibility and trust

 - Proven ability to define metrics and data contracts that multiple teams actually adopt

 - History of building trust and adoption for self-serve data products, not just building them

 - Systems thinker who sees how a modeling decision ripples through dashboards, reports, and (increasingly) AI agents

 - Ownership mentality — comfortable with January's decentralized operating model, and willing to show ownership behavior beyond your formal remit when it serves the broader goal

 - Client-oriented — genuinely curious about what clients need from their data, not just what they ask for

 - Clear communicator who can write documentation people actually read and adopt

Bonus Points:

 - Experience building data products or context layers that also serve LLM-based or agentic consumers

 - Experience with a BI/self-serve tool such as Sigma or Looker

 - Background blending analytics engineering with client-facing or consulting work

 - Previous startup or high-growth company experience

HOW WE WORK

 - Decentralization beats control. The best calls get made by the people closest to them, not routed up a chain. You'll set the standards that let the team decide without you in the room.

 - Speed beats perfection. You run tight loops, act at 70% on reversible calls and adjust as you learn. Fast loops beat slow ones.

 - Candor beats comfort. You'd rather hear a hard truth early than a polite sidestep that wastes everyone's time.

 - Writing beats the average meeting. Clarity scales.

 - AI runs through everything here. 95% of our consumer interactions are AI-driven. Internally, we've built an LLM code reviewer and approver. We benchmark coding agents against real tickets so we can automate more of them. Over the last six months, Engineering has doubled how much we can ship. Non-technical teams are just as fluent in AI - anyone can spin up a custom LLM Slackbot, and everyone consistently builds AI tools and skills that are shipped org-wide.

 - We operate at every altitude. No one here lives only on Mount Olympus, not even the leaders. We get into the trenches to learn the ground truth. We constantly refine our information flows so that our decisions are driven by the best, most up to date inputs.

 - We build in person, at least three days a week in our office in Nolita, with a growing group coming in every day. Random run-ins cross-pollinate ideas. Face time builds trust no thread can. Building alongside people makes work far more fun.
